name: Honeyed Banana Oat Greek Yogurt Protein Bowl
author: Sanae
intro: A morning protein bowl that's easy on the stomach and fast to make. The Greek yogurt and a scoop of whey put it well over 40 g of protein, and you can swap the toppings to whatever you have.
description: Greek yogurt whipped with a scoop of whey, topped with banana, oats, walnuts and chia. Five minutes, no cooking.
steps: Make the base: mix the Greek yogurt with the scoop of whey in a wide bowl until smooth, then spread it flat.
Add the toppings: lay your sliced banana down one side of the bowl. Pour the rolled oats down the opposite side.
Add the crunch: sprinkle the chopped walnuts right over the center where the oats and bananas meet.
Finish: evenly dust the banana slices with chia seeds, drizzle your honey over the entire bowl, and put the mint on top.
storage: Best eaten fresh. To prep ahead, mix the yogurt and whey in a sealed tub the night before and add the toppings in the morning so the oats stay crunchy.
tip: Swap the banana for berries, mango or pear. They all work. The whey is over half the cost, so if it's tight, use a second cup of yogurt instead (you'll lose about 2 g of protein).
image_alt: A bowl of Greek yogurt topped with sliced banana, rolled oats, walnuts, chia seeds and mint

name: One-pot spiced chicken, red lentils and rice

ingredients.label: chicken breast, cut into bite-size pieces

description: Chicken, rice and red lentils simmered together with cumin and smoked paprika. Four dinners from one pot.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the chicken with half the salt and brown it for about 5 minutes. It doesn't need to be cooked through yet.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the onion and cook 4 to 5 minutes until soft, then the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 more minute.
Stir in the rice, lentils, tomatoes with their juice, the water and the rest of the salt. Bring it to a boil.
Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer 18 to 20 minutes, stirring once halfway so the lentils don't catch on the bottom.
Tip in the frozen peas, put the lid back on and leave it off the heat for 5 minutes. Taste for salt and pepper.
Divide between 4 containers.
storage: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. It thickens as it sits, so add a splash of water before reheating.
tip: Red lentils cook in the same time as white rice and do a lot of the protein work for very little money. If it looks dry before the rice is done, stir in another ½ cup of water.
image_alt: Sliced seared chicken on a bed of lentils, rice and peas
image_credit: Similar dish, plated. Photo by Dannie Sorum on Unsplash.

name: Lemon-rosemary chicken with grilled squash

ingredients.label: yellow squash, cut into ½-inch rounds
eggplant, sliced (optional, grill with the squash)

description: Juicy grilled chicken cutlets with squash, green beans and carrots. Two lunches, ready in about 40 minutes.
steps: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally so you have thin cutlets that cook evenly.

Mix 2 tbsp of the oil with the lemon zest and juice, garlic, rosemary, salt and pepper. Turn the chicken in it and leave it 15 to 20 minutes while you do the vegetables (up to 2 hours in the fridge is fine).
Steam the green beans and carrots for 3 to 4 minutes, until they just lose their raw crunch. Rinse under cold water so they stop cooking and don't go soft by day three.
Heat a grill pan or heavy skillet until properly hot. Cook the chicken 4 to 5 minutes, flip, then 3 to 4 minutes more, until the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C). Rest it 5 minutes.
Toss the squash with the last tablespoon of oil and a pinch of salt and pepper, then sear 2 to 3 minutes a side in the same pan.
Split everything between 2 containers, with the pepper slices in a small separate box.
storage: Keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Store the pepper slices separately so they stay crisp. Reheat the chicken and squash; the beans and carrots are fine cold.
tip: Use 1½ tbsp of oil in total instead of 3. You save about 90 calories a serving and lose no protein. Dried rosemary (1 tsp) is cheaper than a fresh pack.
image_alt: Grilled chicken breast with grilled squash, carrots, green beans and lemon slices
image_credit: Photo by Mark DeYoung on Unsplash.

name: 31g-protein pancake
description: One big whey pancake that takes five minutes and keeps you full until lunch.
steps: Whisk the whey, baking powder and cinnamon in a bowl, then add the egg and milk and whisk until smooth. It should look like thick pancake batter; add a splash more milk if it's stiff.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and wipe it with a little butter.
Pour in the batter and cook about 2 minutes, until bubbles show on top and the edges look set.
Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more. Whey batter goes rubbery if you cook it hard, so keep the heat at medium.
Top with the sliced banana (and chopped dates if you're using them).
storage: Best made fresh. You can mix the dry ingredients for the week in jars, so each morning is just egg, milk and a pan.
tip: The whey is about 80% of the cost. A cheaper whey concentrate works too, but check the label: you may get a few grams less protein.
image_alt: A stack of golden pancakes topped with berries and chocolate spread
image_credit: Photo by Fa Barboza on Unsplash. Shown with berries and chocolate spread, which aren't in this recipe.

name: Garlic Paprika Shrimp and Rice Bowl
author: Sanae
intro: A simple, protein-rich meal that's both nourishing and flavourful: savoury garlic, tender shrimp, fluffy rice.
description: Garlicky paprika shrimp tossed through fluffy rice in one pan. Two bowls in about 40 minutes.
steps: Cook the rice: rinse it and cook it in a pot of salted water. Once tender, drain if needed and set aside.
Cook the shrimp: heat the olive oil in a pan. Add the onion and garlic and sauté until fragrant. Add the shrimp, paprika, black pepper, salt and herbs, and cook until the shrimp are pink and opaque.
Combine: add the cooked rice straight to the shrimp pan. Mix gently so the rice soaks up the seasoning, and cook together for another 2 to 3 minutes.
Serve: spoon into bowls and garnish with fresh parsley or coriander. Add a squeeze of lemon if you like, and serve warm.
storage: Keeps up to 2 days in the fridge in an airtight container.
tip: Frozen shrimp works fine here. Shrimp is lower in protein per gram than chicken, so for a bigger protein hit use the whole 12 oz bag (340 g): that takes each bowl to about 30 g of protein.
image_alt: A white bowl of paprika-orange rice and shrimp topped with fresh coriander
